chronicle_entries.base_text: With Cnoc Brezhal pressing hard along the frontier, Seladh had no choice but to marshal what strength remained. Seladh fought as their position demanded: without retreat, without reinforcement, and with the particular stubbornness of a household that understood what defeat would cost them beyond the battlefield.

chronicle_entries.base_text: In the period following a separatist movement, Bazkhul Orghzem entered a span of compounding disorder that no single account has ever fully untangled. Orghek Bazrun's military order deteriorated sharply while civil tensions climbed across Bazkhul Orghzem, and the instability this produced was not the clean disorder of a single fracture but the grinding, directionless kind that comes from too many things failing at once.

chronicle_entries.base_text: The rupture in Vrothmikand, held by Xomul Barath announced itself not with fire, but with silence — old allies ceasing, overnight, to speak the same language. The circulars passed between cells in Vrothmikand were remarkable less for their radicalism than for their grief — written by people who had once believed in the order they now meant to end.

chronicle_entries.base_text: Dhrukun Phezal had governed Kholbazhan for a generation before the ideology that built them began to consume them. What records survive from Kholbazhan describe Dhrukun Phezal's military strength eroded — not as consequence of the revolt, but as its cause. Deprivation had made the theoretical feel urgent and the moderate feel cowardly.

chronicle_entries.base_text: Over the span of a year, the struggle for Tlapal-Bezor, held by Atzzan Hamrul ground on without resolution, each season indistinguishable from the last. Skirmishes in Tlapal-Bezor followed a rhythm that owed more to habit than strategy. Ground was taken and surrendered in the same week, positions traded like debts neither party could afford to settle.

chronicle_entries.base_text: In Hazbok Duzghal, held by Ghazzrak Tharbal, what had begun as decisive action calcified into something worse — a stalemate that consumed resources without producing outcomes. Tension across Hazbok Duzghal remained volatile, though the character of that friction had shifted — less the sharp anticipation of battle than the dull weight of a quarrel no one could finish.

chronicle_entries.base_text: Later chroniclers would mark a labor shortage as the moment Zerun Ghethal, held by Bazkelm Tharunk crossed from crisis into something more permanent. With stability at dangerously unstable levels across Zerun Ghethal, decisions made under pressure proved ruinous. Resources went to the wrong positions, alliances to the wrong parties, and each error compounded.

chronicle_entries.base_text: There were opportunities to arrest the decline in Bazgrun Orghzal, and the historical record is clear that each one was squandered. Over the span of a year, Bazgrun Orghzal shed what had taken generations to build. Granaries emptied, trade routes contracted, and Thokhal Pharvun's commerce diminished and families began leaving the region with a finality that left no ambiguity about what had been lost.

Bazgrun Orghzal that emerged from the crisis bore its old name and little else. What had been broken would be rebuilt, if at all, on entirely different foundations.

chronicle_entries.base_text: What Tharvuzhim had taken generations to build, over the following weeks of sustained pressure was enough to undo. Accounts from Tharvuzhim describe a peculiar stillness — the kind that descends when the outcome is known but not yet spoken. Ghelmul Dhuzhan's military order deteriorated sharply while civil tensions climbed, and those with means to leave had already done so.

chronicle_entries.base_text: The withdrawal from Hazbok Duzghal was orderly in the official dispatches and catastrophic in every other account that survived. The garrison at Hazbok Duzghal held longer than expected. The end came not with a battle but with absence — of supply, of reinforcement, of any sign that relief was possible.

History would record the fall of Hazbok Duzghal in a single sentence. Those who had been present understood, without needing to explain it to anyone, why that sentence was insufficient.
